newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Sixty rebels reported killed in northwest Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Sixty rebels reported killed in northwest Colombia.

text.p: At least 60 leftist guerrillas were killed in fighting and military airstrikes over the weekend in Colombia's northwest province of Antioquia, authorities said on Monday.

Gen. Ivan Ramirez Quintero, army commander in Antioquia, said the dead included at least 25 guerrillas killed in aerial bombardments and fighting that finally managed to break a rebel blockade of a key highway linking central Colombia with the banana-growing region of Uraba. Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels had maintained the blockade in a rugged mountainous area since Monday of last week.
"We've recovered the area with fire and blood and we're not going to let it go," Ramirez told reporters.

Pedro Juan Moreno Villa, a senior official with the Antioquia provincial government, said 35 National Liberation Army (ELN) guerrillas were killed in weekend fighting for control over the small towns of Guarne and Porce.

He gave no details but military sources confirmed that a total of at least 60 FARC and ELN guerrillas had died in the lastest round of fighting across the notoriously violent province where gunmen of the left and right have killed with impunity for years.

The ELN declared a nationwide offensive on Friday against the government of President Ernesto Samper, calling him a puppet of drug lords who was seeking to curry favour with the United States by handing power over to the Colombian military.

A wave of ELN attacks on Monday included the torching of seven tractor-trailer trucks laden with coal and firebombing of at least three other vehicles in northern Cesar province. In Sucre, also in the north, ELN saboteurs dynamited a fuel pipeline and in Cucuta, on Colombia's border with Venezuela, they set fire to a city bus.

The attacks followed Sunday's bombing, also by the ELN, of the 220,000-barrel per day Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline in Norte de Santander province. The pipeline carries oil from the Cano Limon field operated by Occidental Petroleum Corp Plc to the Carribean port of Covenas. It has been attacked 35 times by ELN rebels so far this year and more than 400 times since it opened in 1987.
